title: The Devil

seo.title: Destiny matrix 15 — The Devil: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: Fifteen in the destiny matrix is the energy of desire and matter: where it gives a strong pull and the force to get things, and where it hooks you.

meaning: The fifteenth arcanum is attraction. Fifteen in the destiny matrix means a person is driven by strong, bodily wanting: a pull towards money, towards another person, towards power, towards taste, towards having things at all. This is the most earthly of the major energies — it does not reason and does not wait, it pulls you towards the object like gravity. That is where the power of this number comes from, and its price.

The main engine here is appetite, and appetite is also the main question. The same wanting works as fuel and as a trap: while it belongs to you, you take and you build; the moment it becomes the master, it takes you. The inner conflict of the arcanum is not between wanting and not wanting, but between “I have a desire” and “the desire has me”. The number itself never draws that line — a person draws it again every time.

To carry this arcanum is to live with a constant inflow of force and a constant temptation. Inside there is heat, magnetism, the feeling that you can get what you want if you really want it; and beside it a quiet current that drifts you back to whatever already holds you. People notice someone like this: the fifteenth has a dense presence, others follow and believe. Emptiness and half-measures are unbearable — where there is no taste and no thrill, a dull tension builds up.

Fifteen at its strongest stays the owner of its own pull rather than its servant: it turns hunger into work, magnetism into the ability to lead, and takes what it wants without growing into it for good. The weak one is ruled by the pull: the thing wanted becomes a leash, and all the force goes into holding on to what is already held. The difference is not in how much a person wants, but in which of the two is in charge.

Next to its neighbours the fifteenth differs by temperature. The fourteenth, Temperance, dilutes and balances and waits for the right proportion — The Devil thickens and takes at once, because measure bores it. The sixteenth, The Tower, is the collapse of what was held for too long; the fifteenth is exactly what builds up the attachment that The Tower later brings down. The Devil is about the chain and its sweetness, The Tower about the moment the chain breaks.

article.title: Arcanum 15 in the destiny matrix — The Devil: the power of desire and its price
article.short: 15 in the destiny matrix is The Devil, the arcanum of desire and attachment. It brings a strong “I want”, a firm grip on money, magnetism and a feel for what drives people — and it tests you with a single question: do you run your desire, or does it run you? Fifteen turns up in the matrix of 82% of people, most often in the point just below the centre, where the karmic tail and the relationship line begin. In the centre of the chart itself, this number never appears.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 15: The Devil — meaning, karmic tails and money
seo.description: Destiny matrix 15 is The Devil, desire and its price: why it is never in the centre, where 82% of people do have it, its tails, money and love.

sections.h2: What 15 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: Most arcana describe what a person is like. The fifteenth describes what pulls at them and what holds them. It is the energy of desire that has weight: the pull towards money, the body, taste, power, a particular person, the very feeling of “this is mine”. Where 15 stands in a chart, a person wants for real — not “that would be nice”, but so strongly that desire becomes the engine.

Hence the strength of the number. Someone with a vivid fifteenth arcanum knows what they want and does not pretend that money or pleasure leave them cold. They throw themselves in to the point of thrill, hold out under a load that makes others give up, and understand people well: what they want, what they are afraid to lose, what they are ready to do for it. Such a person gets noticed; their presence is dense, and people follow them.

Hence, too, the price. Desire that knows no measure slowly changes its owner. First you want, then you need, then you cannot do without. Benebell Wen, author of Holistic Tarot, names the Devil’s mechanism precisely: a “preference for instant gratification over delayed gratification”. “Now” beats “later” again and again, and a person ends up bound to a situation they would never have chosen. That is why 15 is the arcanum of dependence in the broad sense: not only on substances, but on a person, a salary, approval, the feed on your phone, the sense of control, the need to be needed.

Attachment has two sides. You can be the one who is held, or the one who holds: through money, guilt, jealousy, through knowing someone’s weak spots. The fifteenth arcanum describes both roles, and the second is no freer than the first. Whoever keeps hold of another has to keep holding all the time — watching, checking, never letting go.
**15 gives the power to want and to get. Its lesson is to remain someone who can say no.** Not forever and not on principle, but at any moment when desire starts running you.

The name is frightening, but there is no verdict in it. Wen says plainly that the card is “not a literal beast or demon”: it “personifies human selfishness and indulging in that selfishness”. Even Arthur Edward Waite, the man behind the best-known tarot deck, lists the card’s grim meanings and then adds a proviso: “that which is predestined but is not for this reason evil”. Plus or minus is set not by the number but by how you live with it.

sections.h2: The plus and the minus of 15: how to tell them apart
paragraphs: The plus and the minus of the fifteenth arcanum are not two different people but one and the same force in different hands. The easiest way to see it is in everyday scenes.

head: Area
15 in the plus
15 in the minus
rows: Money
Names the price plainly and earns where others are too shy to sell
Lives from purchase to purchase, borrows to have it now
Desires
Knows what they want and says it out loud
Wants everything at once; “later” does not exist for them
People
Sees motives and negotiates so that both sides win
Presses on the weak spot, holds people through guilt, money or need
Intimacy
Passion, honest talk about desires, acceptance of the partner’s dark sides
Jealousy, control, “you’re mine”, a bond held together by attraction alone

Drive and stamina, gives it everything
Cannot stop, or spends years in a job they hate for the sake of the money
Shadow
Not afraid to talk about the shameful, helps others get out
Cynicism: “everyone has a price, nobody does anything for free”

paragraphs: The last row is the hardest to notice. Wen sees in the Devil not only the pull towards pleasure but also a bleak view of the world: “extreme negativity, distrust, and faithlessness”, the belief “that no positive outcome can possibly come from such a world”. This is the flip side of the number’s main talent. Someone who reads other people’s motives well risks no longer believing that anyone ever acts without one. Then insight turns into suspicion, and knowing people into contempt for them.

A pause test helps to tell desire from dependence. Can you put off what pulls at you — a purchase, a meeting, overtime, checking someone else’s phone — for a week, without panic and without taking it out on anyone? If you can, it is your desire, and it serves you. If the very thought makes you anxious or angry, you are no longer the one choosing.

sections.h2: Where 15 comes from and where it leads: 6, 14 and 16
paragraphs: Add up the digits of fifteen: 1 + 5 = 6. The sixth arcanum is [The Lovers](/encyclopedia/arcanum/6), the card of choice. Wen sets the two side by side: “Key 6 is about one choice”, between virtue and desire, while the Devil is “the aftermath of having abandoned virtue and indulged in desire” — when that choice has hardened into a way of life. Six asks “what should I choose?”; fifteen asks “what is already choosing for me?”

An example. Taking on a side job to pay for a holiday is a choice — that is six. Discovering three years later that you are scared to drop the side job, and the holiday never happened, is fifteen. Hence the way out: take the choice back where it has long been making itself. Not banning, but deciding again — consciously, every time. How the two energies work together in one chart is covered on the page for the [combination of 6 and 15](/encyclopedia/combination/6-15).

The neighbours in the sequence show where 15 sits in the larger story. Before it comes [Temperance, 14](/encyclopedia/arcanum/14): measure, blending, the right proportion. The Devil is what happens when measure is lost: “just a little more”, “one last time”, “I’ll stop later”. After it comes [The Tower, 16](/encyclopedia/arcanum/16): the collapse of what was held on to for too long. Measure, excess, collapse. The fifteenth arcanum is the last point in this sequence where you can still step out of excess on your own, before life breaks the structure from outside.

sections.h2: Where 15 appears in the matrix, and where it never does
paragraphs: Fifteen is one of the most common arcana in the matrix: 82.1% of people have it in at least one position of the reading (for the other arcana the share ranges from 13.4 to 85%). If you have found 15 in your own chart, you are in the majority, and there is nothing sinister about it. What matters more is where exactly the number stands. The shares below are calculated across all birth dates from 1900 to 2026.

paragraphs.h3: Why 15 never appears in the centre

paragraphs: People ask this a lot, and the answer is arithmetic. The centre E is A + B + C + D, where the bottom point D is itself A + B + C. The sum of the three numbers of the date goes into the centre twice, and after reduction it gives one of sixteen numbers: 3–14, 16, 18, 20 or 22. Fifteen is not among them, and neither are 1, 2, 17, 19 and 21. For the same reason 15 never appears in Manipura: that chakra’s row repeats the centre.

If you see 15 next to the centre in your chart, it is almost certainly point M — it sits just below the centre, on the way to the bottom point D, and one person in four has 15 there. Less often, 15 turns up in the other inner points: K above the centre, J to the left, L to the right. If a calculator has put 15 right in the centre, it is using a different formula, and its result departs from Natalia Ladini’s classic scheme.

paragraphs.h3: How to find 15 in your chart without a calculator

paragraphs: Most of the places where 15 can stand are easy to check in your head. You need three numbers: your birth day A (if it is over 22, add its digits: 27 → 9), the month B and the sum of the digits of the year C (if that is over 22, add again: 1999 → 28 → 10).

ul: **Born on the 15th** of any month — 15 is your calling card.
**Born in 1905, 1914, 1923, 1932, 1941 or 1950** — 15 is in the material task C.
Add A + B + C. **A sum of 29** — 15 below the centre and the karmic tail [15-8-11](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-8-11).
**A sum of 26, 35, 44 or 53** — 15 below the centre and the tail [15-5-8](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-5-8).
**A sum of 5, 23, 32, 41 or 50** — 15 below the centre and the tail [15-20-5](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-20-5).
**A sum of 24** — 15 in the middle of the tail [9-15-6](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-15-6).
**A sum of 15** — 15 in the karmic task D and the tail [18-6-15](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-6-15).

paragraphs: Example: 31.03.1993. Day 31 → 3 + 1 = 4, month 3, year 1 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 22. The sum 4 + 3 + 22 = 29: fifteen stands below the centre, and the tail is 15-8-11. The other positions — talents, money, family line, purpose — take a few more additions and are easier to work out in the calculator.

sections.h2: The point below the centre: gateway to the tail, relationships and Svadhisthana
paragraphs: Fifteen’s most common place is [point M](/encyclopedia/position/comfort_south), between the centre and the karmic task D. Only multiples of three ever appear here, and 15 is the most frequent of them all: 23.5% of people, almost one in four.

Three lines start from this point at once. The karmic tail runs from M down to D. The relationship line runs from M to the “under the heart” point and on to where it crosses the money line. And in the chakra map, M is the energy of [Svadhisthana](/encyclopedia/chakra/svadhisthana), the level of joy and creativity. So for a quarter of people the Devil stands where desire, intimacy, joy and an old script meet. That is why 15 shows up in the chakra section more often than in any other section of the reading — for 43.6% of people.

M describes the first reaction at the moment a situation becomes personal. With 15 that reaction is “I want” and “mine”. In the plus it is a lively, warm, bodily attraction: the person does not hide their interest, knows how to enjoy things, catches fire easily and sets others alight. In the minus it is a grip: hold on, lock it down, make sure it will not leave. Nothing has been decided yet, but the hand is already clenched.
Fifteen in M always comes from one of three “centre + karmic task” pairs. The pair decides what exactly the desire holds on with, and which tail the person has.

head: Centre E
Karmic task D
Tail

rows: 10, The Wheel of Fortune
5, The Hierophant
Prohibition: the pull grows stronger when it is forbidden
7, The Chariot
8, Justice
A vow: a union or a family rule quietly turns into a cage
4, The Emperor
11, Strength
Power: pressure takes on the look of lawful right

paragraphs: Fifteen sits in the karmic tail of 28.1% of people. There are five such tails out of the 26 possible, and the number’s place in the triple changes its role. At the entry, 15 is the first impulse that sets the circle going. In the middle, it is what keeps the circle turning. At the end, in the place of the karmic task, it is where the circle leads.

ul: [15-20-5](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-20-5) — 10.1%, the most common tail of all. The pull is stronger than the rule, and the answer to a ban is rebellion; the task is to choose an order you serve of your own accord.
[15-5-8](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-5-8) — 9.2%. A union, a vow or a family rule turns into a loss of freedom, and the reckoning comes as a trial, outer or inner.
[15-8-11](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-8-11) — 4.2%. First the grip, then “I’m within my rights”, then the blow in return; the task is a strength that has no need to press.
[9-15-6](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-15-6) — 3.4%, the only tail with the Devil in the middle. What is kept secret gains strength and starts to hold on; the task is to choose love openly.
[18-6-15](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-6-15) — 1.3%, the only one where 15 stands at the end. Enchantment becomes a bond, the bond becomes captivity; the task is to learn to let go.

paragraphs: A karmic tail is only the triple in the M–N–D position. The same numbers on another line do not count as a tail. Someone born on 31.03.1993 has the tail 15-8-11 and the relationship line 15-20-5, and the second triple is read as the couple’s script, not as a karmic tail.

sections.h2: 15 in a couple and in compatibility
paragraphs: In the relationships section, 15 appears for 32.9% of people — most often through the same point M where the relationship line begins. Fifteen brings strong attraction, physicality and a wish to be together for real into a couple, and its main risks are jealousy, control and trading freedom for comfort. Good relationships for this number are the ones where both people could leave and stay of their own free will. More on the pages [15 on the relationship line](/encyclopedia/position/relations/15) and [15 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/15).

Compatibility is more complicated than tables like “15 goes well with 3 and 6, badly with 4 and 9” promise. The method has no list of matching and clashing arcana, and 15 makes no one incompatible with anyone. Compatibility is read from the couple’s matrix: the matching points of the two charts are added together and reduced to a number from 1 to 22. Yuliana Lisovskaya described this approach in detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (The Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024).

In a couple’s matrix, 15 can land in the centre — something impossible in a personal chart. It happens when the partners’ centres add up to 15: 7 and 8, 6 and 9, 5 and 10, 4 and 11, or 3 and 12. For Lisovskaya, the couple’s centre is the shared atmosphere, what goes on between two people away from view. With 15 in the plus, it is passion, open talk about desires, acceptance of each other’s dark sides and powerful support. The author adds a caveat: even in the plus, one partner may want to possess the other, and resentment and jealousy follow. In the minus, attraction alone holds the couple together, and pressure, control and attempts to keep the other person through money, status or a child appear.

One more observation from Lisovskaya: in her experience, 15 in the “why we met” point (the sum of the partners’ birth months) very often means breaking free of a dependence. Her closing thought on the fifteenth energy would suit a personal chart just as well: nobody belongs to anybody.

sections.h2: 15 and money: the money channel and the “dollar sign” point
paragraphs: On the [money line](/encyclopedia/position/money), 15 appears at the entry L (4.2%), at the middle point R2, known as the “dollar sign” point after the symbol other charts put there (3.2%), and at the crossing with the relationship line, R (1.9%). All three share one meaning: money comes through desire — your own and other people’s.

At the entry L, fifteen is the first money impulse: a person starts earning where they themselves badly want something, and is not shy about the price. At the dollar sign it is the direction of income: money comes through what other people badly want — pleasure, beauty, status, risk, comfort — and through a knack for selling, negotiating and understanding what the client is really paying for. At the crossing R, money and intimacy intertwine: what is earned becomes the language of the relationship, and the relationship becomes part of the business.

The minus here is easy to spot. Money turns into a hook: a loan to have it now; a purchase to drown out emptiness; a job you cannot quit because of the salary; “I pay, so I decide”. With this number you do not need to learn to want money. You need a rule set before temptation, not during it: a limit, a deadline, a sum after which you stop. A decision made with a cool head protects you from the one that desire would make.

The arcana of the money line do not change with age; experience does. After forty it is usually clear which money brought freedom and which tied you down. More on this in the section [on money after 40](/encyclopedia/position/money40).

sections.h2: 15 in the calling card, talent and profession
paragraphs: [Point A](/encyclopedia/position/day) is what people see in you at first glance. Fifteen stands here only for those born on the 15th — 3.3% of people. The first impression they make is drive and magnetism: they show interest openly, close the distance fast, and around them you start wanting something. The strength is honest desire: with such a person it is clear what they are after. The flip side is the temptation to use charm as bait and to test how far they can go.

On the talent line, 15 stands at the [inner point K](/encyclopedia/position/comfort_north) (7.6%) or at the middle point P (4.6%). It never reaches the first point of the line, B: that is the birth month. The talent of fifteen is understanding desire, your own and other people’s: what a person really wants, what draws them, what they are afraid to lose. It is the ability to see what others prefer not to mention — money, power, attraction, dependence — and to work with it without squeamishness.
That is why 15 feels at home in work that involves strong desire and calls for a cool head:

ul: finance, investment, trade, a business of your own;
psychology, work with addiction and crises;
law, security, investigation — anything where you need to see hidden schemes;
the pleasure and beauty industries: food, fashion, cosmetics, entertainment;
work with the body: sport, dance, massage.

paragraphs: These are directions, not a prescription. There is one sign that the talent is working in the plus: the person on the other side gets what they really wanted, not just what they could be hooked on.

sections.h2: Purpose, programs and the family line
paragraphs: Most often, 15 lands in the [spiritual purpose](/encyclopedia/position/harmony) — for 13.6% of people. Less often in the planetary (7.4%), personal (4.3%) and social (1.8%) purpose. At the level of purpose, fifteen speaks no longer of pleasure but of a task: to know the power of desire and dependence from the inside and to learn to handle it so that it serves rather than owns. The strong version is a person who knows first-hand how unfreedom works and can therefore help others out of it: at work, in the family, or simply by example. Money, power and pleasure are for them neither a forbidden subject nor an end in themselves.

People who search for “15 program” usually mean scripts that repeat in circles. In the reading, the [programs](/programs) section reads the karmic task D, the centre E and the spiritual purpose. Fifteen never appears in the centre, so in this section it comes in through D or through the spiritual purpose — for 14.9% of people in all. The script of fifteen follows one recognisable path: get, get attached, fail to let go, and pay with freedom for what once brought joy. A program does not mean this will happen. It means this is your most well-worn path, and it switches on by itself when you are tired, frightened or bored.
If 15 stands in the karmic task D, your centre is always 3, The Empress, and your tail is 18-6-15. The root task here is learning to let go of what you love without ceasing to love it.

In the family lines, 15 appears in points F (5.5%), I (4.9%), G (4.1%) and H (2.8%). Here the number speaks of how the family dealt with money, pleasure and power. The family’s gift is grip, vitality, the ability to earn and not be ashamed of prosperity. The family script worth noticing is love expressed through control, money as a way of holding on, a habit handed down in the family as the norm. The script is not necessarily yours, but it helps to know it: that makes it easier not to repeat it out of inertia. More in the section [on the gifts of the family line](/encyclopedia/position/family_gifts).

In the material task C, fifteen stands for those born in 1905, 1914, 1923, 1932, 1941 and 1950. The same point feeds into the section [on the body’s resource](/encyclopedia/position/body_resource): here 15 gives dense, physical energy and recharging through pleasure — taste, movement, intimacy. The task is to enjoy pleasure without turning it into the only way of coming back to yourself.

On the matrix’s age scale, each ten-year span is led by one outer point. Fifteen can lead childhood up to 10 (point A), the years from 10 to 20 (F), from 30 to 40 (G), from 40 to 50 (C), from 50 to 60 (H), from 60 to 70 (D) and from 70 to 80 (I). The decade from 20 to 30 falls on the birth month, so 15 never appears there. A decade under the fifteenth arcanum comes up for 24.2% of people.

Such a period is usually one in which desires speak louder: money, the body, passion, power, ambition. In these years it is easy to pile things up — connections, commitments, habits, possessions — and it becomes especially clear which of them start to hold you. The decade-by-decade reading is in the section [on the age scale](/encyclopedia/position/years), and if you are interested in 15 as the energy of a single year, there is a [separate page](/year/15) for that.

sections.h2: The Devil in the Waite tarot: what is on the card and how to read it
paragraphs: Next to this section is the classic card from the Rider–Waite deck. Pamela Colman Smith drew it to Arthur Edward Waite’s design, and the deck came out in 1909. In The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Waite explains the card’s symbols, and most modern readings rest on this drawing.

Above the scene is a creature Waite calls “the Horned Goat of Mendes”: goat’s horns, “wings like those of a bat”, a bird’s claws. It is perched on a dark altar. The right hand is raised with the palm open — in Waite’s words, “the reverse of that benediction which is given by the Hierophant”, the fifth arcanum. The left holds “a great flaming torch, inverted towards the earth”. On the forehead is a reversed pentagram, and on the belly the sign of Mercury.

Two figures are chained to a ring on the altar — a naked man and woman with small horns and tails. Waite likens them to “Adam and Eve after the Fall”: “Hereof is the chain and fatality of the material life.” The tails stand for the animal nature, but “there is human intelligence in the faces”. The pair echoes the Lovers card. There an angel stands above Adam and Eve; here, the Devil. There a tree of flames stands behind the man and a tree of fruit behind the woman; here the man’s tail ends in fire and the woman’s in a bunch of grapes. The same two people, only now outside the garden gate.

The most important thing Waite says is about the one sitting above them: “he who is exalted above them is not to be their master for ever. Even now, he is also a bondsman, sustained by the evil that is in him and blind to the liberty of service.” In this reading the Devil’s power is neither absolute nor eternal, and the one who holds the chain is bound no less than those he holds. Waite reads the figure itself as “the Dweller on the Threshold without the Mystical Garden” — the one met by those driven out for eating the forbidden fruit.

Modern readers add a detail that Waite does not mention but that can be seen in the drawing: the loops of chain around the necks are wide enough to lift off over the head. Nobody is holding these two by force — they stay of their own accord.

The image did not take shape at once. In the earliest surviving hand-painted decks of the fifteenth century, including the famous Visconti-Sforza deck, there is no Devil: the card was either lost or never part of the set. In the Tarot de Marseille, the Devil stands on a pedestal, with two small demons tied to it by their collars. The card got its goat’s head and torch after 1856, when Éliphas Lévi published his Baphomet — Waite himself notes the influence. Papus replaced the demons with naked human beings, and Smith and Waite brought it all together into a single scene and tied it to the Lovers.

In a spread, Waite gives the upright card these meanings: “Ravage, violence, vehemence, extraordinary efforts, force, fatality” — along with that same proviso about the predestined not being evil. Reversed, it stands for “Evil fatality, weakness, pettiness, blindness.” Wen reads the reversed Devil differently: as “the removal of bondage”, sometimes with a bitter sense of defeat after the break. The destiny matrix has no reversed positions: a number has no top and no bottom.

In the system of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, to which both Waite and Smith belonged, the Devil corresponds to Capricorn and the Hebrew letter Ayin, “eye”. Wen also links the card to Capricorn (22 December – 19 January) and to the element of Earth. She recalls Mara, the tempter who tried to lead the Buddha away from enlightenment: resisting him, the Buddha touched the ground and asked the earth to bear witness to his defeat of Mara — that is, of his own inner demons. None of this enters into the destiny matrix calculation: the zodiac sign plays no part in it, only the numbers of the date.

Fifteen does not need to be “worked through” until it disappears: desire is its fuel, and without it the number loses its strength. The task is more modest and more practical — to make sure you are the one in charge.

ol: **A pause instead of a ban.** Pick whatever holds you more than anything else and put it off for a week. Watch not whether you managed, but what rises up in the empty space: anxiety, boredom, anger. That is exactly what the attachment was covering.

**Name the function.** Ask not “how do I quit?” but “what does this give me?” — calm, a sense of strength, the feeling of being alive or needed. Until the function is named, one attachment simply takes the place of another.
**Say your desires out loud.** Fifteen is most dangerous in silence: an unspoken desire looks for detours — a hint, manipulation, resentment. A spoken one becomes something you can agree on.
**Rules before temptation.** A spending limit, working hours, boundaries in a relationship are decided in a calm state and written down. Rules do not get written in the middle of temptation.

**Check whom you are holding.** Where do you keep someone through guilt, money, being indispensable, jealousy? Loosen one such tie and see what remains. What stays without being held is the real thing.

**Give the force a legitimate field.** Sport, a business of your own, negotiations, passion in a relationship by mutual consent, risk with limits set in advance — the fifteenth arcanum needs a place where it can want at full strength.

**Do not be shy about asking for help.** If this is a real dependence — on drink, gambling, debt, a person — the matrix is no substitute for a specialist. Turning to one is also an act in the spirit of 15 in the plus: admitting what holds you and choosing the way out.

paragraphs: The strongest version of the fifteenth arcanum is a person who knows the power of desire from the inside, has grown into nothing for good, and can therefore afford to want big. There is no need to rescue them from money, passion and power: they know how to handle them.
